distinguishing_features: Mechanical design change to gear tooth geometry (asymmetric helical flank curvature) rather than a monitoring/detection scheme
Redistributes Hertzian contact stress away from the pitch line to reduce pitting nucleation
Alters the physical contact-stress field rather than inferring damage from existing vibration, thermal, or motor-current telemetry
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce pitting fatigue initiation at the gear pitch line by relocating the peak contact stress to a region of lower sliding velocity and thicker oil film, without changing material or adding sensors.
parsed.viable_reason: Asymmetric flank curvature is a physically plausible, testable geometric modification with a stated measurable strain-reduction threshold, using standard materials and already-recorded telemetry.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art proposes altering tooth geometry to shift the contact-stress peak; all three are monitoring/inference schemes, so the geometric stress-redistribution mechanism is a non-obvious departure.
